pricing.heading: How you pay
pricing.summary: Online tools: free credits on sign-up, then you pay per use in credits. Desktop apps: some are free, the others are a one-time licence. Nothing is a subscription. Full prices and terms are on the Pricing page (in English).

free.a: You can start for free. Every new account gets {credits} credits, which cover {swaps} photo face swaps ({faceCredits} credits each), {headswaps} Nano HeadSwap Pro head swaps or {edits} AI photo edits. Results from face swap, head swap and video carry a NanoPocket watermark until the account has bought credits once. Three desktop apps are free: Nano FaceSwap, Nano FacialEdit and Nano ImageTryon.

items.q: Do I need a powerful computer?
items.a: Not for the online tools: they run in any modern browser, on a computer or a phone, and the work happens on our GPUs. The desktop apps do need one: most require Windows 10 or 11 and an NVIDIA graphics card. The memory each app needs is listed on the /trust page.

items.q: Do my photos and videos leave my computer?
items.a: With the desktop apps, no: they stay on your disk and the model runs on your GPU. With the online tools, your files are sent to our GPUs to be processed and are kept only for a short time, so you can download the result. They are not used to train models. The details are in the privacy policy at /privacy (in English).

items.q: Can I swap any face I like?
items.a: Only a face you have the right to use: your own, or that of someone who has agreed. Do not publish swaps of real people without their permission.

items.q: Is NanoPocket the same as Nano Banana?
items.a: No. NanoPocket is an independent product at nanopocket.ai and has no connection to Nano Banana or to other services with a similar name.

video.title: AI Video Face Swap Online, Free to Try: Swap a Face or a Head, Keep the Sound
video.description: Online video face swap: upload a video and a photo of a face, and only the person you pick gets the new face or whole head. Everyone else and the original sound stay as filmed. {grant} free credits on sign-up let you try a short clip first.
video.h1: AI video face swap: only the person you pick changes
video.lead1: Upload a video and a photo of a face, then click the person to change. The face or the whole head is replaced in every frame, while everyone else, the background and the original sound stay as filmed.
video.lead2: Since version 2.0 it runs a new engine built for footage with lots of movement, such as dance. Steep angles, things crossing the face and fast spins all hold up, and face swapping is about twice as fast. New in 2.5: Headswap Fast, the whole head, about 40% faster and about 35% fewer credits than Headswap Best. {grant} free credits on sign-up let you try a short clip first.
video.accountNote: You need a free NanoPocket account. The studio's screens are in your language. Last checked: {date}
video.newHeading: The engine since 2.0: built for movement
video.newBody: Dance is the hardest footage for a face swap: heads tilt back, hair and sleeves sweep across the face, the camera spins and the stage lights change colour. The engine works out again for every frame where the face is, which way it points and what is in front of it. In each pair below, "Original" is the source video and "{version}" is the result, made from one reference photo with no manual masks or keyframes. This engine is used by the face swap modes Fast and Best quality; head swaps have their own modes, Headswap Best and Headswap Fast.

features.title: Hands, hair and sleeves over the face
features.body: What is in front of the face is worked out frame by frame. It stays as filmed, and the features behind it do not show through.

features.title: Steep angles, heads tilted back, even upside down
features.body: A head tilted back until the face points at the sky, a shot from below, a turn to full profile: the new face stays with it and is there as soon as the face returns.

features.title: Fast spins and motion blur
features.body: Even when a spin blurs the frame, the swap does not flash back to the original face.

features.title: In a group dance, only the one you pick
features.body: Through crossing paths, camera cuts and leaving and re-entering the frame, it stays with the same dancer. If two people are equally prominent, it asks you to choose instead of guessing.

features.title: Stage light and smoke
features.body: Purple light, orange light, smoke, a dark stage: the new face takes on the light of the scene, so it does not look pasted on.

features.title: Glasses, closed eyes, extreme close-ups
features.body: Glasses stay sharp and keep their colour, eyes close when the original's do, and close-ups are steadier (frame-to-frame flicker down by up to 34%).

video.precisionHeading: Up close: where the earlier engine went wrong
video.precisionBody: In each pair, "Before 2.0" is the earlier engine and "{version}" is the new one: the same footage, the same reference photo, the same frame.

angle.title: One face, even with the head tilted back
angle.look: Look at the cheek beside the nose. With the head back and fingers at the mouth, the earlier engine misplaced the face and put an extra eye on the cheek. Now the face sits firmly in place.

hand.title: A hand over the face
hand.look: Look at the back of the hand. The earlier engine let the outline of the nose and cheek show through it. Now the hand is whole, and only the visible part of the face is swapped.

video.clipsBody: All of these are real output from {name}. The footage and faces come from free stock libraries (Pexels, Mixkit) and are for testing only.

profile-turn.title: A turn to profile and back
profile-turn.body: The head turns ninety degrees and back. Every angle has the new face, with no flicker during the turn.

hand-glasses.title: A hand in front of the face, and glasses
hand-glasses.body: The hand stays in front of the face untouched, and only the visible part of the face is swapped. When the hand moves away, the face is complete at once.

arm-across.title: An arm sweeping across the face
arm-across.body: The head is turning, the camera is shaking and an arm passes in front of the face, yet the face does not jump.

head-back-hands.title: Laughing, with hands in the hair
head-back-hands.body: Hands touch the face and hair, and the head goes back with the laugh. The swap keeps up the whole way.

profile-back.body: A side view in very low light, then a turn towards the camera. The face stays on the head throughout.

faq.q: Is video face swap free?
faq.a: You can start for free. Every new account gets {grant} credits once, enough to try a short clip. After that, each video is paid for in credits. There is no subscription, and the cost is shown before you start.

faq.q: How long can a video be?
faq.a: Up to 60 seconds in Fast and Best quality, and up to 12 seconds for head swaps. Our GPUs are limited, so an account that has never topped up makes clips of up to 5 seconds (3 seconds for head swaps), and these wait behind those of accounts that have. A longer video is not refused: the studio uses the first part or the part you choose, and tells you which before you pay.

faq.q: Why is there a watermark on my video?
faq.a: Videos from an account that has never topped up credits carry a slowly moving, semi-transparent NanoPocket mark. After one top-up, the videos you make have no watermark. Free sign-up credits do not count as a top-up, and a finished video keeps the mark it was made with.

faq.q: What is the difference between a face swap and a whole-head swap?
faq.a: A face swap replaces only the face and keeps the original hair, head shape and expression, which suits talking, interviews and longer clips. A whole-head swap takes the face, hair and head shape from the reference photo and leaves the body, clothes, background and other people alone, which suits short shots.

faq.q: Can I swap any face I like?
faq.a: Only a face you have the right to use. The studio asks you to confirm this before it starts. Do not publish face swap videos of real people without their permission.

faq.q: What happens to my uploaded video?
faq.a: The studio states that uploads are deleted within 24 hours and that a finished video is kept for 24 hours, or 7 days for an account that has topped up. They are not used to train models. See the privacy policy at /privacy (in English).

faq.q: Is the studio in my language?
faq.a: Yes. The studio's screens are in your language.

faq.q: How is it different from Nano FaceStudio Online?
faq.a: Nano FaceStudio Online runs in the browser on our GPUs and is paid per use in credits. Nano FaceStudio Pro is a desktop app with a one-time license that runs on your own GPU, has no fee per image, and adds mask edit, expression editing, Face Vivid, upscale, light adjust and crop.

faq.q: Are my photos uploaded?
faq.a: No. Every model runs on your GPU, and your photos are never uploaded or kept on a server. The only network traffic is a one-time license activation.

faq.q: What hardware do I need?
faq.a: Windows 10 or 11 with an NVIDIA GPU and at least 8 GB of VRAM. RTX 30, 40 and 50 series have been tested. The macOS build for Apple Silicon (M2 to M5) is still to come, and Intel Macs are not supported.

faq.q: Can I try it before I buy?
faq.a: There is no trial of the desktop app. You can try the online tools for free first: Nano FaceStudio Online uses the same swap engine, and you get free credits when you sign up.

faq.q: Can I use the results in client work?
faq.a: Yes, under the Terms of Use, which are in English. Using someone's likeness without their consent is prohibited.

pricing.title: Prices: free apps and pay-per-use credits
pricing.description: Free desktop apps, online tools paid per use in credits, and one-time Pro licenses. Face swap from {face} credits a face, photo edit {edit} credits. No subscription.
pricing.lead: Three ways to pay, and none of them is a subscription. The free desktop apps cost nothing. The online tools are paid per use from a credit balance, where 100 credits is one US dollar and the price is shown before you start. The Pro desktop apps are a one-time license.
pricing.onlineHeading: Online tools: pay per use, in credits
pricing.onlineNote: These run on NanoPocket's GPUs in your browser, so nothing is installed. If a render fails or is cancelled, the credits are returned. Credits never expire.
pricing.faceStudioPay: Face swap {face} credits per face; head swap {head} credits.
pricing.faceStudioNote: Up to {faces} faces in one photo. Face detection is free. You pay per face replaced, so faces you leave alone cost nothing.
pricing.headswapNote: Swaps the whole head: face, hair and head shape. Up to {variations} variations a run; each costs the same, and a failed swap costs nothing.
pricing.videoPay: Priced per video from the mode, output size, clip length and number of people, and shown before you start.
pricing.videoNote: A 10-second 1080p clip in Fast mode is about 20 credits. Requests are queued.
pricing.imageEditNote: Lossless PNG at full resolution. Accounts that have never bought credits get a watermark. Every pixel outside the edit stays identical.
pricing.packsNote: Buy credits when you need them. 1 credit is $0.01, and bigger packs add bonus credits. Credits are bought on the credits page.
pricing.freeNote: A new account starts with {grant} credits. An account that has bought credits is also topped up to {topup} credits whenever it runs low; one that has never bought gets no top-up. Free credits are limited to one account per person.
pricing.watermarkNote: The watermark: renders from {video} and Nano FaceStudio Online made on an account that has never bought credits carry a NanoPocket.ai watermark. Buy credits once, with any pack, and it is removed from the renders you make afterwards. Free credits do not count as buying.
pricing.desktopHeading: Desktop apps: free or a one-time license
pricing.desktopNote: The desktop apps run on your own NVIDIA GPU on Windows, so your photos and videos stay on your computer. A license is separate from credits.

faq.q: Is there a subscription?
faq.a: No. The online tools are paid per use from a credit balance you top up when you want to, and the desktop apps are free or a one-time license.

faq.q: Do credits expire?
faq.a: No. Credits never expire, and the price of each render is shown before you start. If a render fails or is cancelled, the credits are returned.

faq.q: Do credits work in the desktop apps?
faq.a: No. Credits pay for the online tools only. Desktop licenses are separate: buying credits does not affect a license, and holding a license does not use credits.
